stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. If
$\{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ is a covering of the site
$\mathcal{C}$, then the morphism of presheaves of sets
$$
\coprod\nolimits_{i \in I} h_{U_i} \to h_U
$$
becomes surjective after sheafification.
hypotheses:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. If
$\{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ is a covering of the site
$\mathcal{C}$,
conclusions:
the morphism of presheaves of sets
$$
\coprod\nolimits_{i \in I} h_{U_i} \to h_U
$$
becomes surjective after sheafification.

reason: A map h_U#→F is a section of F(U). By the sheaf separatedness axiom, a section restricting equally on all U_i is unique, so the sheafified coproduct of the representables is epimorphic by the cited sheaf epi criterion.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $E \subset \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ be a
subset such that every object of $\mathcal{C}$ has a covering by
elements of $E$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of sets. There exists a
diagram of sheaves of sets
$$
\xymatrix{
\mathcal{F}_1 \ar@<1ex>[r] \ar@<-1ex>[r] &
\mathcal{F}_0 \ar[r] &
\mathcal{F}
}
$$
which represents $\mathcal{F}$ as a coequalizer,
such that $\mathcal{F}_i$, $i = 0, 1$ are coproducts
of sheaves of the form $h_U^\#$ with $U \in E$.

$$
which represents $\mathcal{F}$ as a coequalizer,
such that $\mathcal{F}_i$, $i = 0, 1$ are coproducts
of sheaves of the form $h_U^\#$ with $U \in E$.

reason: Form F_0 as the coproduct over test objects U in E and sections s∈F(U) of h_U#, mapping via their universal sections. Covering-generation ensures the map F_0→F is epi. Cover the kernel pair F_0×_F F_0 by another such coproduct F_1, and apply the canonical kernel-pair coequalizer theorem.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of sets on
$\mathcal{C}$. Then there exists a diagram $\mathcal{I} \to \mathcal{C}$,
$i \mapsto U_i$ such that
$$
\mathcal{F} = \colim_{i \in \mathcal{I}} h_{U_i}^\#
$$
Moreover, if $E \subset \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ is a subset such that every
object of $\mathcal{C}$ has a covering by elements of $E$, then we may
assume $U_i$ is an element of $E$ for all $i \in \Ob(\mathcal{I})$.

reason: The first claim is shown by the category of elements of F: colimit of representables evaluates bijectively on every object via (X,t,id_X), and sheafification preserves the colimit. But the source explicitly omits the second claim, that the entire diagram can be chosen with all U_i in an arbitrary covering-generating subset E (line 2514). The reviewed theorem asserts both.
